title: Consolidate streaming auth refresh + unified backoff across SDKs; opt-in Go connection pooling
author: Lina Park
description: Context: Our Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs diverged in how long-lived streaming connections handle token refresh, transient errors, and ergonomic iteration patterns. This caused intermittent stream resets, duplicate token refreshes under expiry storms, and developer confusion when porting examples between languages. Motivation: provide a single mental model and operational behavior across SDKs so product teams can rely on predictable streaming semantics and SLO-friendly retry/backoff defaults. What this PR does: centralizes token refresh logic behind a shared AuthRefresher interface (Python/TS) and a token watcher goroutine (Go), serializes refreshes per-connection to eliminate race conditions, introduces a uniform exponential-with-jitter backoff policy for streaming retries (special-cased to honor streaming idempotency), exposes a StreamIterator in TypeScript with parity to Python's iterator/async-iterator ergonomics, and adds an opt-in connection pooling toggle in the Go SDK to reduce TCP churn for high-connection-count clients. Compatibility: Default behavior is backward compatible; new behaviors opt-in via client option flags or environment toggles. Checklist: - implement AuthRefresher adapters in each SDK - wire backoff policy into streaming loop with metrics hooks - add TS StreamIterator wrapper and docs examples - add Go pool as opt-in with sane defaults and metrics - augment e2e and perf tests; update changelogs and bump SDK versions. Migration notes: existing usages continue to work. To opt in: Python/TS: pass auth_refresher or use SDK default; Go: set REDWOOD_GO_CONN_POOL=true or pass ClientOptions.UseConnPool=true. Tradeoffs: serialized refresh reduces redundant token calls but can add small latency when many connections refresh simultaneously; connection pooling reduces connection setup cost at the expense of shared connection lifecycle semantics (documented). Rollout plan: canary on internal integration clusters, gated release with perf lab smoke tests, immediate revert patch available if regression detected. Testing summary: unit tests, integration streaming tests, and perf microbenchmarks were added; CI run passed after a single flaky streaming test re-run.

review_conversation: Omar: Overall looks good. We should add a metric for token-refresh-waits so we can detect serializer-induced latency — please add.
Lina: Added token_refresh_wait_ms metric and dashboard link in the perf canary README; added a test that asserts it appears after simulated expiry.
Priya: TypeScript StreamIterator ergonomics look cleaner. Minor: prefer names 'stream.nextChunk()' vs 'stream.next()' for clarity.
Lina: Renamed to nextChunk() to avoid collision with JS iterator semantics; updated examples.
Ben: Go pool opt-in is good but ensure connection leak scenarios are covered — add finalizer and context cancellation propagation.
Lina: Added finalizer and explicit Close behavior; added integration test that asserts no goroutine leaks under 10k short-lived connections.
release_notes: SDKs: unified streaming auth-refresh semantics and standardized transient-error backoff. TS: new StreamIterator API for parity with Python. Go: opt-in connection pooling to reduce connection overhead. Bumped Python/TS/Go SDK versions. No breaking changes by default; opt-in flags for new behaviors.
notes_for_backport: Backport to release/1.13.x (python) and release/0.9.x (typescript) recommended for customers hitting repeated stream resets; Go pool is optional and can be omitted from stable backports.
